body.p: The AI Positron add-on provides access to the AI Positron side-view. If the view is not displayed, it can be opened by selecting it from Window Show View .

fig.title: Clickable Image Map of the AI Positron View

body.p: The top header stripe contains the following actions and menus:

dd.p: Clears the information in the chat pane and start a new chat.

dlentry.dd:
Displays up to 20 conversations. Pinned conversations appear first, followed by the most recently changed unpinned conversations in the remaining slots. Pinned conversations are ordered from newest to oldest. Recent conversations never displace pinned conversations. If more than 20 conversations are pinned, only the 20 newest are displayed. Hover over a conversation to view its description in a tooltip and display its pin and rename buttons. Click the pin button to pin or unpin the conversation without closing the menu. Click the rename button to open the Rename chat dialog box, where you can enter a new title in the Title field. The rename button is unavailable while the AI generates the title and description for a new conversation. Each time a conversation is saved, it moves to the top of the unpinned recent conversations. Conversations that no longer fit in the menu remain available in the Chat History dialog box.
The menu then provides the following actions:
Show all history - Opens the Chat History dialog box where you can find, organize, open, export, import, or delete project conversations.
Export project history... - Exports the history for the entire project.
Import project history... - Imports the history for the entire project.
Clear history - Clears the chat history.
Export chat... - Exports the current conversation.
Import chat... - Imports the current conversation.

Contains the available AI-powered actions that can be used to generate and refine content. You can use the Search actions button at the top of the menu to help you quickly locate a particular action. Simply select an action to trigger it. You can hover the mouse cursor over an action to see a description of what the action does. The Record examples button allows you to create custom actions or prompts by recording changes. The next section contains a list of the 5 most recently used actions.

dlentry.dt: Open in separate window toggle button
dlentry.dd:
Moves the entire AI Positron view from the side view to a separate maximized window. You can then restore, resize, or move the window to a second monitor. In this window, the conversation text and chat input box are displayed slightly larger.
While AI Positron is open in a separate window, the button changes to Dock back into side view. Use this button to dock the assistant back into the side view, or simply close the separate window.
While AI Positron is open in a separate window, its chat history is displayed in a panel to the left of the chat. Click a conversation to open it. The conversation currently open in the chat is highlighted. In the separate window, click the Show history button to display the chat history panel. When the panel is visible, the same button changes to Hide history. Click it to hide the panel. While the AI is processing a request, the list is disabled. You cannot select or open conversations, but you can still search them. You can right-click one conversation and select Rename to edit its title in the list. The current title is selected. Type the new title and press Enter to keep it or Escape to cancel. If the AI begins processing a request while you are renaming a conversation, the rename is canceled.

Shows the status of the Oxygen MCP server and the number of documents modified by external AI assistants through the server that are awaiting review. The number appears on the icon. Click the icon to review the changes. For details, see Server Status and Changed Files.

This menu contains the following:
My account (available only for AI Positron Service connections) - Opens a webpage where you can see your current subscription package and credit status.
Disconnect (available only for AI Positron Service connections) - Disconnects Oxygen from the Oxygen Positron Service.
Preferences - Opens the Oxygen AI Positron preferences page where you can configure various options, including the AI Positron service address and the Context for the user that the AI will use to create more relevant and personalized responses.

body.p: Before a conversation has been initiated, the main response pane contains general instructional information and links to quickly change the chat mode. You can also click the Show actions link to see a list with all available predefined AI actions.

Once a conversation is initiated, this pane presents the results after processing an action and allows you to further refine the responses by sending messages to the AI service. When an AI Positron action is triggered, the response pane displays the progress and results.

Responses are received from the server in streaming mode (the AI sends chunks of the response as it is being generated rather than waiting to send the entire response after it is generated). Depending on the received response, AI Positron may switch the response visualization between the following modes:
Text (with syntax highlight for XML, Markdown or other content types) - You can open links from the response area in a web browser by hovering over the links, then holding the Control/Command key and mouse click.
Markdown (HTML) - The Markdown response is converted to HTML as it is received and displayed in a browser-like UI that supports styling for code blocks, links, tables, lists, headings, and inline elements (bold, italic, underline, and code phrases). You can easily copy the contents of a code block by clicking the Copy button in the top-right corner. For security reasons, this response does not load or display embedded remote resources (e.g. images).
Author - If the response contains XML content, AI Positron may switch the response to be viewed in an Author mode renderer, similar to how that same received XML content may be rendered in the main editor area.

Before the response (to the far right), there is a horizontal ellipsis (Switch how the response is rendered drop-down button) that allows you to switch between visualization modes and also to disable auto detection and choose a mode to be used preferentially.

An AI validation agent performs automatic fixes when the AI model responds with an XML document that is invalid according to the associated document type. If the response XML is not well-formed, it is also automatically fixed by the agent.

Once the entire response is received from the server, the following actions could be available under or next to the response (depending on the type of AI action):
Insert/Replace - Inserts the response at the cursor location within the document (or replaces the selected content). If the insertion generates validation errors in the document, the AI model receives the validation errors and attempts to fix the problems.
Preview - Opens the built-in file comparison tool where you can preview the content that would be inserted at the cursor location within the document. You can choose to preview the comparison in either Text or Author mode. If the insertion generates validation errors in the document, the AI model receives the validation errors and attempts to fix the problem.
For actions that create and modify files and save the changes to disk, a Waiting for approval box is displayed below the response and above the chat input area.

The modified files are displayed in a collapsible list. Modified files have a star icon () while new files have a plus icon (). You can double-click a file to open it in the built-in file comparison tool where you can review the modifications. The changes are already applied to the file. To retain them, click Keep changes; to revert them, click Undo changes.

The following actions are available in the Waiting for approval box:
Keep all - Keeps the changes in all listed files.
Undo all - Reverts the changes in all listed files.
Review changes - Opens the particular file in the built-in file comparison tool where you can review the modifications.
Keep changes - Keeps the changes in the particular file.
Undo changes - Reverts the changes in the particular file.
The Review changes, Keep changes, and Undo changes actions are also available from the contextual menu when right-clicking a file.

You can also start chatting with the AI directly in the chat input box at the bottom of the view. You can invoke an existing action directly from the chat input box by providing general instructions to the AI. For example, to invoke the Correct Grammar action, you could type something similar to the following in the chat input box:Invoke the action to correct grammar in the current document and update the document based on the resultsYou can drag (or copy) files (or folders) from your system file browser or screen captures and drop (or paste) them in the chat input box, or you can use the dedicated Attach action in the top of the chat input box. For more details, see .

You can retrieve and reuse a previously sent message, revise it if needed, and then resend it. To restore a message:
With the cursor in an empty input area, use the Up arrow keyboard button to show the previous message. Its attachments are also restored. Press Up again to go further back.
With the cursor at the end of the text, use the Down arrow keyboard button to navigate forward through the messages. After the most recent one, the input area is empty again.

If the chat displays a conversation (including if it was opened from the chat history), the messages come from that conversation. If the chat is empty, they come from the conversations in the history, starting with the most recently changed message. When you reach the end of the conversation's messages, Up continues with the next older conversation.Text that you typed yourself is never replaced. The Up and Down arrows only move the cursor. If you edit a retrieved message, the navigation stops. If you start a new chat, open another conversation, or switch to another version of an edited message while browsing, the input area goes back to how it was before you started browsing.

You can search for available AI-powered actions by using the Ctrl + Space keyboard shortcut within the chat input box. Actions in the dynamic filter results match your search based on their title or description (visible in the tooltip on hover).
To invoke an action from the filtered list, either double-click on the item or press Enter.
At the top of the chat input box, the following buttons are available:

dlentry.dd: Adds a prompt as a stored favorite.

Use this menu to select one of the supported variables:
${selection} - Expands to the currently selected content.
${selection-original} - Expands to the currently selected content. If the current selected content contains track changes, they are rejected, resulting in the original version of the text.
${selection-final} - Expands to the currently selected content. If the current selected content contains track changes, they are accepted, resulting in the final version of the text.
${document} - Expands to the content of the entire document.
${attach(filePath)} - Attaches a specified image (in png, jpeg, or svg format) or XML, Markdown, text, Word (.docx), Powerpoint (.pptx), Excel (.xlsx), or PDF file to the conversation. For Word and PDF files, the included images are also sent to the AI engine.

dlentry.dt: Start recording prompt using the microphone button
dlentry.dd: Allows you to record your voice, which is converted to a text prompt using the AI engine. After starting the recording, the button is changed to a Stop action that you use to stop the recording.
Use this action to attach files or images to the conversation. For details, see Attachments.

body.p: The bottom header stripe contains the following actions and menus:

dlentry.dd: Allows you to change the chat mode (Agent, Ask, DITA Agent, Planner, Personas). For more details, see Chat Modes.
Opens a dialog box where can filter and choose which tools (either added via Model Context Protocol or provided in the chat mode definition) to use for the conversation.
This menu allows you to select from the available AI models to be used for chat purposes and for actions that do not explicitly specify a model.

dd.p: The circular progress bar on this button shows the approximate fill level for the model's usable context window for the next request.

Hover over the button to see specific details such as the percentage of the usable context window that is filled and the current and total token counts. For external AI connections, it also shows the token count for the last response and a running total for the whole conversation (including any responses regenerated or replaced by edits). For Oxygen AI Positron Service connections, it shows the percentage of your plan's credits used, the exact credit count, and the date your credits reset.

Click the button to compact the current conversation. A confirmation dialog box verifies if you want to continue. When compaction occurs, the AI creates a hidden summary of the conversation to reduce the context that will be used by future requests. You can click the resulting visual marker that notes the conversation has been summarized to preview the summarized recap.
If the Auto-compact conversation option is enabled in the Preferences dialog box, the conversation is automatically compacted before you send a new message whenever the context exceeds 70%.

dlentry.dd: Use this button (or Enter) to send your prompt to the AI. While the request is being processed, this button becomes a Stop that can be used to stop the processing.
